report.verdict: A dental office administrator with retail management experience, shown through titles and dates alone.
write_up: You’re an office administrator at Harlow Dental Group, with retail work before that. This is a common profile pattern: the jobs have titles and dates but no descriptions. A recruiter knows where you worked, not what you did, and is likely to move on.

Your move from Sales Associate to Assistant Store Manager at Brightway is worth keeping visible. It shows a change in role, but neither job says what you handled. There isn’t a job description to use as a model yet.

Start with the Harlow job: add the office work that’s yours and who relies on it. Then update the headline and About, followed by the Brightway management job. A recruiter could then compare your dental office work with the job they’re filling.

cards.line: Office Administrator at Harlow Dental Group
cards.cannot_tell: This repeats your current title without saying what you manage. Put the dental setting and your office work beside the role.
cards.example: Office Administrator | Dental Group | [office work you manage]
cards.question: What office work is yours at Harlow Dental Group?

cards.cannot_tell: A recruiter has no introduction to your work before reaching the job titles. A short first-person opening can say what you do at Harlow.
cards.example: I work as an Office Administrator at Harlow Dental Group. I [office work you manage] for [who relies on your work].
cards.question: What do you manage at Harlow, and who relies on that work?

cards.line: The Office Administrator job at Harlow Dental Group has no description.
cards.cannot_tell: The dental office job is the first place a recruiter will look for your current work, but the title is all they have. Start with the responsibilities that are yours.
cards.example: [The office work you manage] for [who relies on that work].
cards.question: Do you handle the schedule, billing, the front desk or something else at Harlow, and how many dentists or patients do you support?

cards.where: Brightway Home Goods, Assistant Store Manager
cards.line: The Assistant Store Manager job at Brightway Home Goods has no description.
cards.cannot_tell: Your move into management is visible, but what you managed at the store isn’t. Add the work that belonged to you.
cards.example: [The store work you managed], including [a named responsibility].
cards.question: Did you run the schedule, open and close the store, handle the cash office or manage other work? How many people were on a shift?

cards.cannot_tell: Teamwork doesn’t name the office work or systems you use. The three skills shown are Microsoft Office, Teamwork and Communication; use those places for the work your target job turns on.
cards.example: [Dental office system you use] | [administrative method you use] | [retail management skill you use]
cards.question: Which office systems, administrative methods or store management skills have you used in these jobs?

fit.why: Your headline and current title both name office administration at Harlow Dental Group, with retail management before it.
fit.level: mid-level, your current title is Office Administrator
fit.note: 'Office Administrator' is in your headline and current title. 'Dental Group' is in your headline and employer name. 'Assistant Store Manager' is in your earlier experience, and 'Microsoft Office' is among your top skills. Someone hiring a dental office administrator may also search for scheduling, insurance verification and billing; those terms aren't on your profile. Add the ones you do, and bring the most relevant one into your headline.
